title: Backtest Golden Case v1
description: One curated golden case for the Knowledge PTalk RAG backtest. A golden case is a hand-pinned (subject, grade, book, volume, page, current_lesson) context + a student utterance + the EXPECTED retrieval outcome. Golden cases are the deterministic, version-controlled subset (Layer 2 'golden routing' in docs/backtest/methodology.md), distinct from the Gemma-generated ~500-per-book cases (Layer 3 'full sweep'). Field semantics mirror rag_edu/scripts/schema_v3_2026_06/backtest_book.py so a golden case can be replayed against /retrieve with the same scoring (anchor = norm(work_name)==norm(expected); guard = tier not in CARD_TIERS).

id.description: Stable unique id. Convention: <subject>-<grade>-<book_set>[-t<volume>]-<seq>, e.g. 'toan-4-CTST-007'. Must be unique within a golden set and stable across runs (used to join before/after in compare_runs).

grade.description: Lớp / grade. SGK range covered today is 4-9.

volume.description: tap_no (1 or 2) when the book is split into volumes, else null. CRITICAL for volume-collision: page numbers reset between tap 1 and tap 2, so volume must scope page lookups (see invariant 'Không trùng tập 1/2').

page.description: trang the speaker says they have open (the 'trang' the client passes, or a page named in the utterance). null when the case carries no page context.

current_lesson_id.description: The client-supplied current_lesson context (work_name or lesson key the speaker is sitting on). This is the #1 structured anchor in the routing chain (current_lesson -> name -> trang+tap -> content-vector). null simulates the 'client sends {}' degraded case.

utterance.description: The raw student-voice query sent as `query` to /retrieve. Keep it natural (may omit diacritics / be teen-speak) to mirror real ASR output.

intent.description: What the student is trying to do. Drives expected `mode`/tier. 'chitchat'/'offtopic'/'out_of_scope' imply should_refuse=true.

expected_node_id.description: Ground-truth target. The :Lesson.work_name that MUST be anchored (compared via norm() == norm()). null when should_refuse=true (a correct refusal anchors nothing). For non-refusal cases this is required (enforced by allOf below).

expected_tier.description: Optional expected serving tier for `mode` scoring. One of the CARD_TIERS for answerable cases, or a non-card tier ('none'/'noncard') for refusals.

in_scope.description: True if the requested content actually exists inside (subject, grade, book_set, volume). False for out-of-book / cross-grade / out-of-page-range probes.

should_refuse.description: True if the correct behavior is to NOT emit a lesson card (guard case). Scored like backtest_book.py guard: pass = returned tier not in CARD_TIERS. When true, expected_node_id should be null.

tags.description: Free-form labels for slicing (e.g. 'long_math_title','volume_collision','trap_year','title_norm'). Used by reporters.py slice tables and to target known weak slices.

notes.description: Optional human note: why this case exists, which regression it pins, source of ground truth.
